$comment: Tunable QA rules read by scripts/auto-qa-tuner.mjs (run by .github/workflows/auto-qa.yml). The tuner reads recent GitHub Actions runs and proposes follow-ups (fix a flaky workflow, investigate failures, raise a timeout). It never edits this file or any workflow and never commits: proposals go to a tracking issue and a human applies them. Edit the numbers here to tune it.

rules.failure_rate_threshold: A workflow is flagged when failed or timed-out runs divided by completed runs (success, failure, timed_out) in the window exceeds this fraction. Cancelled and skipped runs are ignored.
rules.flaky_rate_threshold: Runs are grouped by workflow, commit and event. A group is flaky when it has both a failed and a successful run, or a successful run whose attempt number is above 1 (`gh run list` shows only the latest attempt, so a re-run that passed appears this way; a re-run of a cancelled run is over-counted). A workflow is flagged when flaky groups divided by groups exceeds this fraction.
rules.slow_p95_minutes: A workflow is flagged when the 95th percentile of successful run durations exceeds this many minutes. The proposal is ceil(p95 * timeout_headroom_factor) rounded up to a multiple of 5, as a timeout-minutes value to compare with the workflow file.
rules.min_runs: Workflows with fewer completed runs than this in the window are reported as insufficient data and are never flagged. Names in `workflows` that match no run (for example a workflow that is not merged yet) are reported the same way.
